summary: Per-instance true/false holder: stores one boolean locally, optionally latching new values until a Set signal fires.
description: Boolean holds a single true/false value that belongs to this node instance alone — it is not named or shared (for an app-wide named value use Variable2). The `value` input sets it and `savedValue` (Value) reads it back. While the `saveValue` (Set) signal input is unconnected, values written to `value` apply immediately; once `saveValue` is connected the node latches: incoming values are held pending and only applied when Set fires. Incoming values are cast with JavaScript Boolean(). `changed` fires only when the stored value actually changes; `stored` fires after every Set trigger, changed or not.
whenToUse: Use it for a local flag inside one component — 'has clicked', 'panel expanded' — especially the latch shape (pin `value` to true, fire Set from a signal) that turns a momentary signal into a level. For state shared across components use Variable2 + Set Variable; for multi-state logic use States.

ports.value: Boolean value input. Applies immediately while Value is ticked under Run On Value Change (the default); untick it to hold the value until Set fires.
ports.saveValue: Signal; applies the most recently received `value`, then reports Done or Unchanged. Connecting it switches the node from pass-through to latch mode.
ports.savedValue: Boolean level with the currently stored value; wire to inputs like `visible` or `enabled`.
ports.changed: Signal; fires only when the stored value actually changes, not on every Set.
ports.done: Signal; a Set stored a value the Variable was not already holding.
ports.unchanged: Signal; a Set stored the value it already held, so nothing changed. ⚠️ With Value left ticked under Run On Value Change this is the common case, because Value has already stored by the time Set fires — untick it if you want Set to be the only thing that writes.
ports.completed: Signal; fires after every Set, whatever the outcome. This is what the old `Stored` port meant, and it replaces it. ⚠️ A Value that wrote straight through reports nothing at all — that is not an invocation of Set.

patterns: Latch a signal into a level: set `value` to true in parameters, wire the signal to `saveValue`, and read `savedValue` — a sticky 'this has happened' flag.
`savedValue` → Condition `condition` to branch signal flow on the stored flag.
antiPatterns: Using two Boolean nodes in different components to 'share' a flag — each instance has its own value and they never sync. Use Variable2 for shared state.
